title: Could You Live Here?
intro: Explores the renovation potential of existing buildings through new uses and adapted programmes. Combining building inventory, generative AI, planning and regulatory analysis, and assessments of economy and climate impact, the project develops and compares feasible scenarios within existing structures. A detailed case study of Instrumentet 17 in Örnsberg investigates how a 1950s and 1960s building can accommodate new ways of living and working.

items.title: Instrumentet 17
items.description: A cellular office interior in Instrumentet 17, with a regular concrete frame, modest window openings, parquet floors, radiators and a layered fit-out accumulated over time. The structure is robust, but the rooms are enclosed and daylight is uneven.

items.title: Brightness
items.description: A former office becomes a calm, generous apartment with wide views over Stockholm. The original structure and window rhythm remain legible, while new surfaces, windows and carefully integrated services make the space feel bright, quiet and distinctly residential.

items.title: Chalet Chaleureux
items.description: The cellular office is opened into a generous loft where the existing columns and window rhythm give the home its character. New floors, windows and built-in joinery and wooden beams add warmth and order, while the larger rooms allow a relaxed way of living.

items.title: Plainly Raw
items.description: A restrained loft conversion that leaves traces of the former office visible. Selected walls are opened up, while the existing windows, radiators and structure remain. Cleaned concrete, simple finishes and a generous open room give it an informal, lived-in character. It's yours to make.

items.title: Shared City Room
items.description: A bright shared home organised around a generous kitchen and dining room. The existing structural frame and window rhythm remain, while new herringbone floors, built-in storage and refined finishes make the common spaces warm, calm and domestic.

items.title: Concrete Reality
items.description: A modest conversion that works with what is already there. Most walls and windows remain, while surfaces are repaired and simplified. The concrete floor and plain rooms keep the character direct and robust, with residential services added quietly around them.

items.title: Paris Terrace
items.description: Selected walls are removed and larger glazed openings bring in daylight and connect the rooms to an exterior terrace. Raw but with prominence. The existing structure stays visible, paired with simple surfaces and an unfussy residential fit-out.

items.title: Vertical Rhythm
items.description: A generous loft apartment shaped by the existing concrete frame and a more open plan. Enlarged windows and doors bring the city closer, while simple new floors and finishes keep the atmosphere calm, robust and slightly unfinished rather than overly polished. Cool, calm, simple.

items.title: Fully Opened
items.description: The former office opens toward the city through impressively large windows, while warm timber surfaces soften the retained concrete frame. Generous shared rooms feel distinctly domestic, with private spaces and new residential services fitted carefully around the existing structure.

items.title: Mixing
items.description: The apartment keeps the irregular character of the former office rather than smoothing everything away. Old and new windows sit together, simple surfaces reveal parts of the structure, and a small balcony adds a direct place to step outside above the city.

items.title: Balcon Filant
items.description: A large room becomes the everyday centre of the home: a place to eat, work, read and gather without losing the building’s concrete character. The finishes stay robust and informal, while a new balcony and improved openings bring more light and outdoor life.

items.title: Walk Outside
items.description: The shared room opens almost wall-to-wall toward the balcony, turning the city view into part of everyday life. The old concrete frame remains present, but new glazing, warm finishes and built-in elements make the interior feel generous, settled and distinctly domestic.

items.title: Your Luxury
items.description: The apartment is organised around a bright living room opening to a new balcony. The original frame remains quietly present, while new windows, warm finishes and built-in storage make the former office feel settled and comfortable without erasing where it came from. Some simple luxury.

items.title: Straight Edge
items.description: Much of the room stays recognisably close to the existing building: the windows are repaired, the structure remains and selected walls are opened. New residential functions are inserted quietly, leaving a spacious home with a direct, robust character.

items.title: Factory Feeling
items.description: The conversion relies on repair rather than replacement. Existing windows, surfaces and room proportions remain part of everyday life, with only a few walls opened and the necessary residential functions added. The result feels simple, spacious and deliberately unpolished.

items.title: It's Yours to Read
items.combinedTitle: s093 It's Yours to Read (Standard Apartment)
items.description: The former office becomes a generous apartment organised by a few carefully placed walls and built-in storage rather than a completely open plan. The existing facade rhythm remains, while renewed surfaces and joinery make the rooms practical, calm and distinctly domestic.

items.title: Cleared Structural Bay
items.combinedTitle: s732 Cleared Structural Bay (Open Plan Office)
items.description: The former cellular workplace is opened into a broad, flexible office floor. Renovated windows and the existing structural rhythm remain visible, while cleaned surfaces, improved lighting and a small number of new partitions create a bright and adaptable place to work.

items.title: Cut Slab, Larger Windows
items.combinedTitle: s395 Cut Slab, Larger Windows (Loft Living)
items.description: Larger windows and changes to the slabs give the former institutional interior a new sense of space. The structural frame remains exposed and the finishes stay deliberately simple, creating a generous loft where rough surfaces and new residential elements sit comfortably together.

items.title: Raw Frame, Built-In Edge
items.combinedTitle: s024 Raw Frame, Built-In Edge (Raw Living)
items.description: The apartment is organised around the existing frame rather than hiding it. Larger openings bring in more daylight, while built-in elements give the rooms storage and definition. Most surfaces remain raw and cleaned, creating a home that feels robust, spacious and deliberately unfinished.

items.title: Cleaned Existing Rooms
items.description: Very little is visually replaced. Existing rooms, windows and surfaces are cleaned and repaired, allowing the character of the building to remain part of everyday life. The new work is quiet and practical, focused on the essential services needed to live there comfortably.

items.title: Opened Office Strip
items.combinedTitle: s137 Opened Office Strip (Open Plan Office)
items.description: The office becomes lighter and more flexible mainly by taking walls away. Renovated windows, cleaned surfaces and the existing frame do most of the architectural work, while modest technical upgrades make the floor comfortable and practical without overbuilding it.
